obtained.how: publisher's open data archive: ESA Ecological Archives E096-202 (the data paper's metadata page and its data files Table1.csv, Table2.csv, Table3.csv and NutrientTraits.zip; MD5 sums match those listed). The Ecology data paper itself is a one-page abstract; the metadata is its full text. Table1.csv and Table2.csv are saved as text beside it (Edwards_etal_2015.table1.txt, .table2.txt) and were summarised with a script

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the archive's landing page
bibliography.note: Edwards, Kyle F., Klausmeier, Christopher A. & Litchman, Elena. 2015. Nutrient utilization traits of phytoplankton. Ecology 96(8): 2311 (data paper; Ecological Archives E096-202-D1); data last updated December 2013.

claims.claim: across 61 freshwater measurements the median half-saturation for P-limited growth was 1.08 µg P/L (IQR 0.45–7.7)
claims.location: web page (metadata), Units and variable definitions; Table1.csv, column k_p_m
claims.conditions: unialgal laboratory cultures, light not strongly limiting, phosphate the single limiting nutrient; Km in µmol/L (× 30.97 = µg P/L); temperatures 5–35 °C; the 61 records cover 28 species, several measured at more than one temperature; system coded 'freshwater'
claims.note: recomputed from Table1.csv: n = 61, median 1.084, quartiles 0.450 and 7.74 µg P/L (R type-7 quantiles), range 0.003–88.6. The median of species means is 0.69 µg P/L; one record coded 'fresh' (Asterionella ralfsii) has no Km

claims.conditions: 25 freshwater diatom records; A. formosa's 7 records 0.006–0.07 µmol/L at 5–20 °C (Tilman 1981; Tilman & Kilham 1976; Van Donk & Kilham 1990; Holm & Armstrong 1981)

a project subset: 14 records of unicellular and small colonial greens (Scenedesmus quadricauda, Chlorella, Chlamydomonas, Oocystis, Sphaerocystis, Selenastrum), excluding Volvox (10 records, 6–89 µg/L) and Scenedesmus obliquus (4 records, 7.7–41)
claims.note: the subset's median is 0.49 µg P/L (range 0.05–5.2). All 27 green records: median 5.2. Excluding S. obliquus is a choice (it is a small green too); with it the median is 0.64. Say 'about 0.5 (0.05–5)' and name the exclusions

claims.source_value: median 3.5 µg P/L over the 8 freshwater cyanobacterial records (0.28, 0.52, 0.88, 1.10, 5.89, 10.3, 20.0, 40.1); 5.9 is the upper of the two middle values (Microcystis aeruginosa, Holm & Armstrong 1981)
claims.conditions: Planktothrix agardhii 4 records (0.28–1.1, Ahlgren 1977, 1978), Microcystis 2 (5.9, 20), Anabaena 2 (10.3, 40.1); 15.5–26 °C
claims.note: the research note's table (copepod_grazing_and_p_kinetics.md §2.1) has the same slip. The spread is bimodal: Planktothrix 0.3–1.1, bloom formers 6–40; 'cyanobacteria 0.3–40 (median 3.5)' or the genera separately would be clearer

claims.conditions: A. flos-aquae 0.3332 µmol/L at 24 °C (Elder & Parker 1984); A. oscillarioides 1.2935 at 26 °C (Lam 1979); Microcystis 0.19 and 0.6452
claims.note: Anabaena 10.3 and 40.1 µg P/L; Microcystis 5.9 and 20.0

claims.quote: Dinobryon sociale var. americanum … chrysophyceae … freshwater … 20 … 0.39
claims.conditions: the only chrysophyte record (Dinobryon) has an uptake K (0.39 µmol/L) but no growth Km

claims.claim: half-saturation for uptake was about 20 times higher (24.8 µg P/L)
claims.conditions: Michaelis–Menten uptake by strongly P-depleted or starved cells only; freshwater, n = 101

claims.conditions: A. formosa at 20 °C, Tilman & Kilham 1976 (J. Phycol.)
claims.note: 0.02 µmol/L × 30.97 = 0.62 µg P/L. The same paper's Cyclotella meneghiniana: 7.74

notes: Script used for the summaries: Python over Table1.csv (CR line endings), µmol/L × 30.973762 = µg P/L, R type-7 quantiles. Other freshwater values: Droop µ∞ median 1.01 d⁻¹ (n = 31); marine Km median 5.1 µg P/L (n = 18). The metadata warns that µ∞ is a curve-fitting parameter that exceeds the attainable µmax.
